content.title: About
content.content: A calzone is a folded pizza made from dough, filled with meat, cheese, and tomato sauce. The crust is usually thin, while the filling stays juicy, making the dish hearty and satisfying.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the Italian word “calzone,” meaning “trouser” or “pocket.”
Traditionally calzones are baked in a wood‑fired oven, but they can also be prepared in a regular home oven.
Unlike open‑face pizza, a calzone is sealed, which helps retain more moisture in the filling.
There are countless filling variations, from classic ham and mozzarella to vegetables and seafood.
In the United States, calzones are often served with marinara sauce for dipping.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The meat provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Cheese contributes calcium, supporting bone and tooth health.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Meat is a good source of iron, important for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both meat and cheese supply B6, B12, and riboflavin, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The combination of dough, meat, and cheese provides a quick source of energy for active days.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Calzones are rich in fats and carbs, so portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese and meat can increase saturated fat intake, which may be a concern for heart health.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Processed meats and cheese often contain a lot of salt; people with hypertension should choose lower‑sodium options.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or dairy protein allergy.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the calzone hot, sliced in half. It can be eaten with hands or with a knife and fork. It pairs well with marinara sauce, a fresh side salad, or a light vegetable side.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months. Reheat until the internal temperature reaches 75 °C.
